chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is reckoned for you when you join them (in congregational prayer), even if you do not follow their recitation, similar to what is reckoned for you when you are with those whose recitation you do follow.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on congregational prayer if I do not follow the Imam's recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the validity and reward of congregational prayer are not contingent upon strict adherence to the Imam's specific recitation style (qira'ah), but rather on the act of joining the community. It underscores the Shia principle of flexibility in ritual practice to preserve unity, ensuring that differences in minor details do not invalidate the collective worship or diminish the individual's spiritual merit.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It would be Reckoned for you when you include yourself with them (in Jam’atal Salāt) and even if you do not follow with them, similar to what would be Reckoned for you when you were with the ones you do follow with’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

It is counted in your favor if you join them even if you do not follow them, just like it is counted in your favor when you are with those whom you follow.’” (Ahadith 5-9 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
